title: Learning juntas from quantum examples

problem.name: Learning juntas from quantum examples
problem.statement_latex: Given uniform quantum examples of an unknown Boolean function depending on at most $k$ of $n$ coordinates, output a classical hypothesis with uniform error at most $\varepsilon$ and constant confidence.
problem.statement_text: Given uniform quantum examples of an unknown Boolean function depending on at most $k$ of $n$ coordinates, output a classical hypothesis with uniform error at most $\varepsilon$ and constant confidence.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial improvement in the stated resource and parameter regime.
strength.description_text: Polynomial improvement in the stated resource and parameter regime.

evidence.description_latex: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.
evidence.description_text: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.

hardware.description_latex: Each example occupies $n+1$ logical qubits. The algorithm additionally needs the indicated number of coherent examples and its measurement/postprocessing workspace; preparing these examples is part of the supplied-access model.
hardware.description_text: Each example occupies $n+1$ logical qubits. The algorithm additionally needs the indicated number of coherent examples and its measurement/postprocessing workspace; preparing these examples is part of the supplied-access model.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(k\log k/\varepsilon)$ quantum examples to identify relevant coordinates, plus $O(2^k\log(1/\varepsilon))$ classical examples to learn the restricted truth table, by Atici--Servedio.
quantum.headline_text: $O(k\log k/\varepsilon)$ quantum examples to identify relevant coordinates, plus $O(2^k\log(1/\varepsilon))$ classical examples to learn the restricted truth table, by Atici–Servedio.

classical.headline_latex: $O((k\log n+2^k)/\varepsilon)$ uniform labeled examples suffice by finite-class learning. Classical search over relevant-coordinate sets can take $n^{O(k)}\operatorname{poly}(2^k,1/\varepsilon)$ time; the information-theoretic sample dependence on $n$ persists.
classical.headline_text: $O((k\log n+2^k)/\varepsilon)$ uniform labeled examples suffice by finite-class learning. Classical search over relevant-coordinate sets can take $n^{O(k)}\operatorname{poly}(2^k,1/\varepsilon)$ time; the information-theoretic sample dependence on $n$ persists.
